title: A purchase order line typed by hand with the old number keeps its number
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test.
  • Create an open purchase order for this test, purchase order 1, from any vendor, with two lines, neither received: one for part A picked from the lookup, and one where part A's number was typed by hand and added as typed, with no link to the part.
  • Use a new part number that no part and no Part Library entry has yet, and that does not contain part A's number.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
  3. Replace the Part Number with the new number.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click Purchase Orders in the left menu.
  6. Open purchase order 1.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 3:

  • Part Number shows the new number.

Step 4:

  • The rename is saved, the window closes and part A's row shows the new number.

Step 5:

  • The Purchase Orders list opens.

Step 6:

  • The line picked from the lookup reads the new number.
  • The line typed by hand still reads the old number: it only shares the number and has no link to part A.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S13-R19a: “A line that only shares the old number, typed in by hand with no link to this part, keeps its number.”
  • S13-R19: “A rename carries over to open work that holds this part, at every location: purchase order lines not yet fully received, part requests not yet received or returned, canned jobs, and returns that are not completed take the new number. A delivery that is not yet accepted is covered by its open purchase order lines. Receiving, ordering, applying a canned job and returning then find the renamed part.”
